title: Remark
body_md:
Both the second-order and fifth-order schemes presented in this section are NOT positivity preserving. 
	We discuss the adjustments to ensure positivity spatially in \S\ref{sec4}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
(Division by a small $c_\alpha$) 
	In the case that $c_\alpha$ is zero or near zero, the divisions within the mass matrix in \eqref{e:massmat} cause it to become ill-conditioned. 
	Hence, to avoid this division by a small quantity, we follow the suggestion of, e.g., \cite{torlo2020} and apply a desingularization; for numerator $n$ and denominator $d$ we take
	
	$$
	\frac{n}{d} \approx
	\begin{cases}
		0, & \text{if } d < 10^{-8}, \\
		\displaystyle \frac{2d \cdot n}{d^2 + \max\{d^2, 10^{-8}\}}, & \text{otherwise}.
	\end{cases}
	$$
	This ensures numerical stability while preserving the physical behavior; see, e.g., \cite{ciallella2022} for more details.

title: Remark
body_md:
For the SW system \eqref{e:sw_vec}, we only apply mPDeC to the $h$ evolution.
	It is physically realistic that the quantity $q$ becomes negative from positive values; thus, $q$ is evolved numerically with the classical DeC.

name: Practical aspects for shallow water

title: Remark
body_md:
In one spatial dimension, \eqref{e:pd_entries} results in the mass matrix $\mathbb M$ in equation \eqref{e:massmat} being a tri-diagonal matrix, barring boundary conditions. 
	In this work, we consider zero-extrapolation, Dirichlet, and periodic boundary conditions; of which, only periodic conditions result in a non-tri-diagonal matrix. 
	In the case where $\mathbb M$ is tri-diagonal, we solve the system with Thomas algorithm.
	In the periodic case, the resulting mass matrix is tri-diagonal with the off-diagonal corners being non-zero.
	In this case, we use a Sherman-Morrison decomposition of the matrix $\mathbb M$ to obtain the solution to $\mathbb M \bm c^{\ell, (m)} = \bm c^n$ explicitly via two separate tri-diagonal solves.

name: Linear solver

title: Remark
body_md: Although we use the Zhang-Shu limiter to spatially ensure positivity, the use of the linearly implicit mPDeC for the time evolution of $h$ allows us to forego its additional strong CFL restriction. In practice, we run the simulations with classical explicit CFL due to the stability of the underlying FD method.

name: Zhang-Shu limiter time-step restriction

title: Theorem
body_md: Given a well-balanced semi-discretization of \eqref{e:fd_semi_disc}, the mPDeC scheme with the semi-discretization in \eqref{e:fd_semi_disc} is well-balanced for the same equilibrium states.
